broken_step: s8 â€” 'The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 6.' This step is simply false as stated: 6^3 - 6 = 210, not 120. It is not a mislabelled-but-recoverable claim either; the unique integer solution of n^3 - n = 120 is n = 5 (bounded search over n in [-200,200] found n = 5 as the only root, and the cubic has at most three real roots so no others exist), so n = 6 does not 'verify' the identity under any reading. s8 is load-bearing in the presented dependency graph: s9 and s10 both depend_on s8, s11 depends_on s10, and the concluding step s12 depends_on s10 and s11. The argument as written therefore routes its conclusion through a false assertion and does not establish the proposition. Two further remarks, offered so the diagnosis is not over-claimed: (a) the conclusion is nonetheless true, and a valid argument is available from the material already present â€” s1 (base case at n=0) plus s2 (5^(n+6) = 5^n mod 7 on [0,74]) plus repeated reduction by 6 suffices, which is exactly what s12 asserts; the defect is that s12 cites s10 and s11 rather than s1 and s2. (b) Steps s4, s7, s10 and s11 are individually true but mathematically inert: none of them constrains 5^n modulo 7, and s4's H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3] is a decoy that is true only because the factor (n-3) annihilates the indicator at the one point where it is nonzero. Inert padding is not by itself an invalidity, so the disposition rests on s8 alone.
